title: Portable Executable Format
description: Read any Windows PE image: the DOS and COFF headers, data directories, sections, imports, exports, base relocations, TLS and resources.
author: Underlayer

exercise_decls.question: What two bytes open every PE file, and what ASCII letters do they spell?
exercise_decls.answer: 4d 5a, spelling MZ
exercise_decls.options: 7f 45, spelling .ELF|4d 5a, spelling MZ|50 45, spelling PE
exercise_decls.explanation: Every PE file starts with the MS-DOS magic 4d 5a ('MZ') at offset 0. 50 45 ('PE') appears later, at the offset stored in e_lfanew. 7f 45 is the ELF magic, not PE.
exercise_decls.hint1: The DOS header comes first; the PE signature is found via a pointer inside it.

exercise_decls.question: Roughly how many layers does a PE file have from byte 0 to section data?
exercise_decls.answer: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, sections
exercise_decls.explanation: The layered chain is: DOS header (with e_lfanew) → DOS stub → PE signature → COFF file header → optional header (incl. data directories) → section table → section data.
exercise_decls.hint1: Start at the MZ header and follow the pointer.

exercise_decls.question: At which file offset does the DOS header store the offset of the PE signature?
exercise_decls.answer: 0x3C
exercise_decls.explanation: The e_lfanew field sits at offset 0x3C (60) in IMAGE_DOS_HEADER and holds the file offset of the 'PE\0\0' signature.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is near the end of the 64-byte DOS header.

exercise_decls.question: A file's bytes at 0x3C are 00 01 00 00 (little-endian). Where does its PE signature start?
exercise_decls.answer: At file offset 0x100 (256)
exercise_decls.options: At file offset 0x0001|At file offset 0x100 (256)|At file offset 0x3C
exercise_decls.explanation: Little-endian 00 01 00 00 = 0x00000100 = 256. e_lfanew is an absolute file offset, so 'PE\0\0' sits at byte 256.
exercise_decls.hint1: Decode the four bytes as a little-endian 32-bit integer.

exercise_decls.question: How many bytes is the IMAGE_FILE_HEADER (COFF header), excluding the 4-byte PE signature?
exercise_decls.answer: 20 bytes
exercise_decls.options: 20 bytes|24 bytes|64 bytes
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER is 20 bytes: Machine(2) + NumberOfSections(2) + TimeDateStamp(4) + PointerToSymbolTable(4) + NumberOfSymbols(4) + SizeOfOptionalHeader(2) + Characteristics(2).
exercise_decls.hint1: Add up the field sizes: 2+2+4+4+4+2+2.

exercise_decls.question: A COFF header has Machine = 4c 01 (0x014C). What CPU does it target?
exercise_decls.answer: Intel 386 (x86, 32-bit)
exercise_decls.options: x64 (AMD64)|Intel 386 (x86, 32-bit)|ARM64
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_I386 = 0x14C is Intel 386 and compatible 32-bit x86. x64 is 0x8664, ARM64 is 0xAA64.
exercise_decls.hint1: 0x14C is the classic 32-bit x86 machine value.

exercise_decls.question: What magic value identifies a PE32+ (64-bit) optional header?
exercise_decls.answer: 0x20b
exercise_decls.explanation: Optional-header Magic 0x10b = PE32, 0x20b = PE32+, 0x107 = ROM image. 0x8664 is a Machine value in the COFF header, not the optional header.
exercise_decls.hint1: PE32 is 0x10b; adding 0x100 gives the 64-bit variant.

exercise_decls.question: Which optional-header field is present in PE32 but absent in PE32+?
exercise_decls.answer: BaseOfData
exercise_decls.options: ImageBase|BaseOfData|AddressOfEntryPoint
exercise_decls.explanation: BaseOfData (offset 24, 4 bytes) exists only in PE32, right after BaseOfCode. In PE32+ ImageBase follows BaseOfCode directly and is 8 bytes wide.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the extra standard field the spec lists for PE32 only.

exercise_decls.question: How big is one data-directory entry, and what does it hold?
exercise_decls.answer: 8 bytes: a 4-byte RVA plus a 4-byte size
exercise_decls.options: 4 bytes: just an RVA|8 bytes: a 4-byte RVA plus a 4-byte size|16 bytes: two RVAs
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY = { DWORD VirtualAddress; DWORD Size; } = 8 bytes. The VirtualAddress is the table's RVA, Size its length in bytes.
exercise_decls.hint1: Two 32-bit fields make 8 bytes.

exercise_decls.question: Why does the Certificate Table entry hold a file offset instead of an RVA?
exercise_decls.answer: Certificates are not mapped into memory with the image
exercise_decls.options: It is a bug in the spec|Certificates are not mapped into memory with the image|The loader needs it before mapping sections
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec says attribute certificates are not loaded into memory as part of the image, so this entry is a file pointer, not an RVA. Everything else in the directory array is an RVA.
exercise_decls.hint1: Think about what the loader maps into memory.

exercise_decls.question: A table is at RVA 0x3A04. Its section (.rdata) has VirtualAddress 0x3000 and PointerToRawData 0x1C00. What is the file offset?
exercise_decls.explanation: file = PointerToRawData + (RVA - VirtualAddress) = 0x1C00 + (0x3A04 - 0x3000) = 0x1C00 + 0xA04 = 0x2604.
exercise_decls.hint1: Subtract the section's virtual address, then add the raw file pointer.

exercise_decls.question: How many bytes is each IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER entry?
exercise_decls.answer: 40 bytes
exercise_decls.options: 20 bytes|40 bytes|64 bytes
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER is 40 bytes: Name(8) + VirtualSize(4) + VirtualAddress(4) + SizeOfRawData(4) + PointerToRawData(4) + 4 more pointer/count fields(10) + Characteristics(4).

exercise_decls.question: A section's VirtualSize is 0x17BC but SizeOfRawData is 0x1800. What fills the gap on disk and in memory?
exercise_decls.answer: Zeros
exercise_decls.options: The next section's data|Zeros|Nothing — the file is truncated
exercise_decls.explanation: SizeOfRawData is rounded up to FileAlignment (0x200 here: 0x17BC -> 0x1800). The spec says if SizeOfRawData exceeds VirtualSize the extra bytes are padding — zeros on disk, zero-fill in memory.
exercise_decls.hint1: SizeOfRawData is aligned up to FileAlignment; VirtualSize is the true length.

exercise_decls.question: What single field in an IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR names the imported DLL?
exercise_decls.answer: Name (offset 12) — an RVA of an ASCII string
exercise_decls.options: FirstThunk|Name (offset 12) — an RVA of an ASCII string|TimeDateStamp
exercise_decls.explanation: The Name field at descriptor offset 12 is the RVA of a null-terminated ASCII DLL name (e.g. 'KERNEL32.dll'). FirstThunk points at the import address table, not the name.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the fourth DWORD of the 20-byte descriptor.

exercise_decls.question: What does the loader write into the Import Address Table during binding?
exercise_decls.answer: The actual memory addresses of the imported functions
exercise_decls.options: The DLL names|The actual memory addresses of the imported functions|The hint values
exercise_decls.explanation: Until binding, IAT entries copy the import lookup table (RVAs of hint/name entries). The loader overwrites each IAT slot with the function's real address — that is what makes calls work.
exercise_decls.hint1: The IAT becomes pointers after the loader resolves each import.

exercise_decls.question: Which export table is sorted so it can be searched with a binary search?
exercise_decls.answer: The export name pointer table
exercise_decls.options: The export address table|The export name pointer table|The ordinal table
exercise_decls.explanation: AddressOfNames entries are ordered lexically to allow binary search. The ordinal table is a parallel array of 16-bit indexes; the address table is indexed directly by ordinal.
exercise_decls.hint1: Lookup by name starts with a search over that table.

exercise_decls.question: In a base-relocation entry, what do the high 4 bits and low 12 bits hold?
exercise_decls.answer: High 4 bits: relocation type; low 12 bits: page offset
exercise_decls.options: High 4 bits: page offset; low 12 bits: type|High 4 bits: relocation type; low 12 bits: page offset|High 8 bits: type; low 8 bits: offset
exercise_decls.explanation: Each 16-bit type/offset word packs a 4-bit type (e.g. DIR64 = 10) and a 12-bit offset within the block's 4K page (Page RVA).
exercise_decls.hint1: 12 bits address up to 4096 bytes — one page.

exercise_decls.question: What does AddressOfEntryPoint contain — an RVA or a VA, and relative to what?
exercise_decls.answer: An RVA — the entry point relative to ImageBase, not an absolute address and not inside main()
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec defines AddressOfEntryPoint as the address relative to the image base. The loader adds ImageBase (plus relocation delta) to get the final VA. It points at process/CRT startup code, not your main() function.
exercise_decls.hint1: 'Relative to the image base' is the spec's wording.

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: which of the three address kinds survives an ASLR rebase unchanged, and which structures keep using it while everything else moves?
exercise_decls.answer: The RVA — data directories, entry point and section VirtualAddresses all store it
exercise_decls.options: The VA — it is the runtime truth, so it must be the stable one|The RVA — data directories, entry point and section VirtualAddresses all store it|The file offset — the file on disk never rebases
exercise_decls.explanation: The RVA is relative to the image base, so rebasing shifts base and item together and the difference stays constant. File offsets are also stable, but they describe the disk, not memory — headers, directories and import records all keep RVAs while VAs move.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: The RVA — data directories, entry point and section VirtualAddresses all store it

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: which two COFF header fields should be zero in a modern image, and why?
exercise_decls.answer: PointerToSymbolTable and NumberOfSymbols — COFF debugging is deprecated
exercise_decls.options: PointerToSymbolTable and NumberOfSymbols — COFF debugging is deprecated|Machine and NumberOfSections — they are implied by the optional header|SizeOfOptionalHeader and Characteristics — images do not need them
exercise_decls.explanation: PointerToSymbolTable and NumberOfSymbols. The specification says both should be zero for an image because COFF debugging information is deprecated — symbols moved to separate debug files.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: PointerToSymbolTable and NumberOfSymbols — COFF debugging is deprecated

exercise_decls.question: A program needs a global counter that several functions increment. Which section of Sample A will the linker place it in, and how do you know from the flags alone — without reading the name?
exercise_decls.answer: .data — it is the only row whose Characteristics include 0x80000000
exercise_decls.options: .rdata, because all data starts in read-only data and is copied later|.text, because mutable state belongs next to the code that uses it|.data — it is the only row whose Characteristics include 0x80000000
exercise_decls.explanation: Only .data carries 0x80000000 (MEM_WRITE): 0xC0000040 = WRITE | READ | CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA. Every other section in both samples lacks the write bit, so the flag — not the four-character name — is what identifies writable storage.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Apply It'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: .data — it is the only row whose Characteristics include 0x80000000

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: what does bit 0 of the delay descriptor's Attributes field decide?
exercise_decls.answer: Whether the descriptor's address fields hold RVAs or raw virtual addresses
exercise_decls.options: Whether the symbols are imported by ordinal instead of by name|Whether the descriptor's address fields hold RVAs or raw virtual addresses|Whether the DLL is already loaded
exercise_decls.explanation: Bit 0 is RvaBased (dlattrRva = 0x1). Set means the Name, Module Handle, Delay IAT, Delay INT, Bound and Unload fields are RVAs; clear means they are raw virtual addresses, the pre-VC7 form.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: Whether the descriptor's address fields hold RVAs or raw virtual addresses

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: a RUNTIME_FUNCTION reads Begin 0x1010 and End 0x1034. Which byte is the last one inside the function?
exercise_decls.explanation: End = 0x1034 is the first byte outside, so the final byte of the function is End minus one = 0x1033, which is exactly where the ret instruction sits.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: in what order do a PE file's layers appear on disk?
exercise_decls.answer: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, section data
exercise_decls.options: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, section data|ELF header, program headers, sections, section header table at the end|Section table first, then DOS header, then section data
exercise_decls.explanation: Correct order: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, then raw section data aligned to FileAlignment.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, section data

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: what does the first dword of the load configuration tell a reader, and why is it first?
exercise_decls.answer: The structure's size, so the reader knows which of the ever-growing fields exist
exercise_decls.options: A set of file-attribute flags, because flags come first in PE structures|The structure's size, so the reader knows which of the ever-growing fields exist|The SizeOfImage of the whole PE
exercise_decls.explanation: It is Size: the structure grew across Windows versions, so a reader uses it as a version gate and only trusts fields that fall inside it. The spec itself says the size is really only a version check.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: The structure's size, so the reader knows which of the ever-growing fields exist

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: a PE file carries IMAGE_FILE_RELOCS_STRIPPED and its preferred ImageBase is already taken. What happens?
exercise_decls.answer: The load fails — the loader reports an error
exercise_decls.options: The loader relocates it anyway using DYNAMIC_BASE|The load fails — the loader reports an error|It loads and only the imports break
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec says a file with relocations stripped must be loaded at its preferred base, and if that address is not available the loader reports an error.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: The load fails — the loader reports an error

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: cli-64.exe loads at 0x140000000 and you see a fault at VA 0x140005008. What is its RVA, and which section is it in?
exercise_decls.answer: RVA 0x5008, in .data
exercise_decls.options: RVA 0x5008, in the file at offset 0x3008 only by coincidence of section deltas|RVA 0x5008, in .data|RVA 0x5008, in .text
exercise_decls.explanation: 0x140005008 minus ImageBase 0x140000000 = RVA 0x5008, which falls inside .data at VirtualAddress 0x5000 — the security cookie slot.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: in a three-level resource walk, which level does the value 0x0409 identify?
exercise_decls.answer: The Language level — it selects English (United States)
exercise_decls.options: The Type level — it selects RT_MANIFEST|The Name level — it selects the instance|The Language level — it selects English (United States)
exercise_decls.explanation: 0x0409 = 1033 is LCID English (United States). Language IDs form the third level, and this entry pointed at the leaf holding the manifest bytes.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: The Language level — it selects English (United States)

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: decode cli-64.exe's DllCharacteristics value 0x8160.
exercise_decls.answer: HIGH_ENTROPY_VA, DYNAMIC_BASE, NX_COMPAT, TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE
exercise_decls.options: FORCE_INTEGRITY plus GUARD_CF|HIGH_ENTROPY_VA, DYNAMIC_BASE, NX_COMPAT, TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE|NO_SEH, APPCONTAINER, and DYNAMIC_BASE
exercise_decls.explanation: 0x0020 HIGH_ENTROPY_VA + 0x0040 DYNAMIC_BASE + 0x0100 NX_COMPAT + 0x8000 TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE = 0x8160, the same four bits objdump lists for this file.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.

exercise_decls.question: Without looking back: whose job is the value stored at Address of Index, and where does it live?
exercise_decls.answer: The loader writes the assigned index there, at load time
exercise_decls.options: The linker writes the final index at link time|The loader writes the assigned index there, at load time|Each thread writes its own index into that slot
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec says the loader assigns the TLS index to the place indicated by Address of Index. The location sits in an ordinary data section so the program can read it by symbol.
exercise_decls.hint1: Re-read the lesson section 'Check Your Understanding'.
exercise_decls.source_quote: The loader writes the assigned index there, at load time
